title: MiraAI POC onboarding labs and success criteria
body:
Purpose and high-level objective:

This doc captures the kickoff plan, experiment matrix, workshop agenda, success criteria and acceptance tests for the MiraAI POC. MiraAI is evaluating Redwood Inference to power clinical note summarization + entity extraction in their clinician workflow. The goal of the 8-week POC is to validate technical fit for a production deployment that meets latency, accuracy, and cost targets, and to produce an operational runbook for the next phase.

POC scope (in-scope / out-of-scope):
- In-scope:
  - Integrate a curated open model via Redwood hosted API for extractive entity extraction and short-form clinical summary generation from structured EHR extracts and free-text notes (up to 2k tokens input).
  - Build a small end-to-end demo: patient note -> Redwood API -> extraction + summary -> UI to display results and allow feedback capture.
  - Run a design-of-experiments across 3 model variants (base, quantized, distilled) and 2 batching profiles (low-latency vs throughput) for cost/latency/quality tradeoffs.
  - Capture per-token cost and latency traces in Redwood Console and export a baseline dataset for quality evaluation (500 de-identified notes).
- Out-of-scope:
  - Full production integration with MiraAI EMR sync or SSO configuration (will be part of Dedicated/private deployment phase).
  - PHI ingestion into Redwood-managed hosted systems until legal sign-off is obtained (we will use de-identified/consented dataset for the POC).

Success criteria (must be measurable):
1) Latency: median end-to-end inference latency <= 350ms per request for the low-latency profile (requests sized <= 512 tokens) measured from API receipt to first token of summary streamed to UI.
2) Throughput/cost: For the throughput profile (batch size 8, 512 tokens), cost per 1k tokens <= $0.60 (hosted API estimate) while maintaining median latency <= 900ms.
3) Extraction accuracy: Named entity extraction F1 >= 0.86 on the 500-note evaluation set (entities: medication, problem, procedure, lab).
4) Summary quality: Clinician-rated average helpfulness >= 4.0/5 across 50 sampled notes in blind review.
5) Reliability: Error rate (HTTP 5xx) < 0.5% and timeouts <= 1% over 72-hour continuous run during stress tests.
6) Observability & reproducibility: Live traces, per-token cost breakdown, and a replayable eval harness (scripts + dataset) are checked into the shared repo and a run produces the same metrics within +/-3% of baseline.

Acceptance tests (executable):
AT-1 (Latency test):
  - Run the low-latency profile for 1,000 synthetic requests (<=512 tokens). Measure median and 95th percentile latencies. Pass if median <= 350ms and p95 <= 900ms.
AT-2 (Cost-throughput sweep):
  - Execute the throughput configuration batch run for 10,000 tokens aggregated. Calculate cost per 1k tokens using Redwood Console billing export. Pass if <= $0.60.
AT-3 (Extraction F1):
  - Run model variant A on the curated 500-note eval set. Compute per-entity and macro F1. Pass if macro F1 >= 0.86.
AT-4 (Human quality check):
  - Blind review by 6 clinicians over 50 notes. Collect helpfulness and accuracy scores. Pass if mean helpfulness >= 4.0 and no systemic safety issues flagged.
AT-5 (Resilience):
  - Run a 72-hour sustained load test with a 15% randomness spike. Check 5xx and timeout rates. Pass if thresholds in success criteria are met.

Experiment matrix (brief):
- Axis 1: Model variant (A = base FP16, B = 8-bit quantized, C = distilled small)
- Axis 2: Batching profile (Low-latency: batch size 1-2, Throughput: batch size 8)
- Axis 3: KV cache enabled/disabled for multi-turn notes
Metrics recorded: latency (median/p95), tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, extraction F1, clinician helpfulness.

Workshop plan (2 half-days) – goal: unblock integration + establish evaluation pipeline
Day 1 (AM): Integration & data prep
  - 09:00–09:15 intro, goals, roles
  - 09:15–10:00 data handoff: sample format, de-identification checklist, schema mapping (MiraAI data engineer + Redwood SE)
  - 10:00–12:00 API integration lab: quickstart into Redwood hosted API, tokenization gotchas, streaming responses demo
  - 12:00–12:30 next steps/actions (data ingest script, S3 location)
Day 2 (AM): Running experiments & evaluating quality
  - 09:00–09:20 recap and experiment plan finalization
  - 09:20–10:30 run a live small-batch test with model A and low-latency profile (observe Console metrics)
  - 10:30–11:15 setup eval harness: how to run reproducible evals and check-ins (GitHub Actions + Console export)
  - 11:15–12:00 UX feedback loop: capture clinician annotations from the demo UI and export to evaluation dataset

Data & access requirements:
- MiraAI to provide 500 de-identified clinical notes in JSONL (fields: note_id, text, created_at, clinician_id (hashed), labels optional).
- If PHI cannot be de-identified for some tests, we will provide a VPC-only private deployment option note and request a short legal/data access path.
- Customer to grant a read-only S3 location or secure file share to Redwood SE for dataset ingestion.

Security & compliance guardrails:
- No PHI will be stored in Redwood hosted systems during the POC without signed DPA and Data Processing Addendum addendum; until then, all POC runs use de-identified data.
- Audit logging will be enabled in the Console for all POC API keys.
- If a Private deployment is requested during POC, reference the Private deployment checklist in linked Confluence doc.

Deployment recommendation (POC -> prod runway):
- POC phase: hosted API (fastest to validate) with strict de-identified controls and short-lived API keys.
- If performance/cost or security constraints push for it, move to Redwood Dedicated with reserved capacity and VPC peering for the production rollout.
- Long-term: Private (customer-managed control plane) if MiraAI needs on-premise or fully air-gapped processing for PHI.

Rollout and canary plan for production (high level):
- Canary 1: 1% traffic on Dedicated pool (non-PHI), monitor latency/cost/quality for 72 hours. Automatic fallback to hosted variant on policy breach.
- Canary 2: 10% traffic with parallel logging to evaluation harness. After stability, ramp to 50% then 100%.
- SLOs: 99th percentile latency target per model profile, error budget of 0.1% per week.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Redwood SE (owner): Aisha Patel — integration, experiment orchestration, evaluation harness setup, runbook draft
- Redwood Solutions Eng: Mateo Garcia — Console dashboards, cost analysis, quantization tests
- MiraAI Lead: Dr. Priya Menon — clinical signoff, clinician recruits for blind review, data owner
- MiraAI Eng: Tom Becker — dataset delivery, UI demo integration

Deliverables by end of POC:
- Evaluated experiment matrix with per-variant metrics (latency/cost/quality)
- Replayable eval harness and dataset (500 notes) checked into shared repo
- Demo UI with streaming summaries and feedback capture
- POC runbook with rollout recommendations and suggested Dedicated sizing

Risk register (top 5) and mitigations:
1) Data delays: MiraAI not able to de-identify notes in time -> mitigation: use synthetic notes + smaller clinical subset to validate pipeline, escalate legal path for partial consent data.
2) Accuracy shortfall: model fails to meet F1 target -> mitigation: run prompt engineering + label-specific calibration, try alternative model variants and retrieval-augmented prompts.
3) Latency spikes under load -> mitigation: tune batching profile, enable KV cache, evaluate Dedicated with reserved GPUs.
4) Billing surprises -> mitigation: set strict quotas on API keys and pre-configured cost alerts in Console.
5) Security sign-off delays -> mitigation: prepare Private deployment checklist and offer short PoC on customer-managed infra if needed.

Open decisions (to finalize during kickoff):
- Final list of 500 notes (which clinics, date windows) and de-identification approach.
- Confirm which three model variants we will test first.
- Whether to run any tests with small amounts of PHI under a temporary DPA amendment.

Questions for MiraAI team:
- Do you have preferred clinician reviewers and a coordinator for the blind review process?
- Is the dataset already mapped to the schema listed above or do we need a mapping session in Week 0?
- Are there internal cost targets that are stricter than the $0.60/1k token baseline?

Immediate next steps (week 0):
1) Onboard 2 Redwood API short-lived keys and attach to demo repo (SE: Aisha).
2) MiraAI to upload a 20-note sample to shared S3 location for quick integration test (owner: Tom).
3) Schedule the 2 half-day workshop (target dates: next Tue/Thu).
4) Prepare evaluation harness skeleton and shared GitHub repo (Mateo).
